title: Responsive Grid Layouts
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of responsive grid layouts.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on responsive grid layouts and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Responsive Grid Layouts helps you build layouts that remain consistent as content, viewport width and component context change.

content_blocks.title: Module 9 learning map
content_blocks.alt_text: Four-step module learning map: Flexbox Fundamentals → Common Flexbox Layout Patterns → Grid Alignment → Troubleshooting Layout Issues. Lesson pages add code examples and practice.
content_blocks.caption: Learning map for Module 9, from the opening concept to a practical checkpoint.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Changing column counts; Adjusting gaps; Responsive card grids; Adaptive dashboards; Combining Grid with breakpoint variants. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Responsive Grid Layouts
content_blocks.code:
<section class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card A</article>
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card B</article>
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card C</article>
</section>
content_blocks.expected_output: Cards stack by default, become two columns at sm, and three columns at lg.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to responsive grid layouts, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Complete the linked practical exercise “Image gallery”. Create a minimal example demonstrating responsive grid layouts. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to responsive grid layouts.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to responsive grid layouts.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: Cards stack by default, become two columns at sm, and three columns at lg.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying responsive grid layouts without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Responsive Grid Layouts is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
